title: Runway Stabilizer: eviction heuristics, tenant 'soft-landing', and high-fidelity telemetry for GPU pools
creator: Ava Martinez
description: After the capacity exhaustion incident on 2026-02-25 we observed rapid GPU pool runway collapse caused by an interplay of KV-cache pollution, tenant surge traffic, and a rigid eviction policy. This ticket implements a 'Runway Stabilizer' feature: a combination of smarter eviction heuristics, a tenant soft-landing policy (graceful degradation to compatible model/route variants) and a set of new telemetry signals to detect runway erosion early. The goal is to reduce hard evictions, keep customer impact contained, and provide clear signals for automated or manual mitigation.
background: Incident summary: sudden tenant surge + KV cache pollution led to queue growth and cascading preemptions. Existing eviction policy used strict slot-count + LRU-style cache eviction which amplified tenant starvation. Gaps identified: no per-tenant runway metric, insufficient differentiation between compute-heavy and KV-heavy requests, and lack of a short-term soft-degrade routing option for tenants approaching eviction thresholds.
proposed_solution: 1) Add a per-tenant 'runway' score that estimates time-to-eviction based on recent slot use, KV-cache hit trend, and outstanding queued work. 2) Revise eviction heuristic to prefer low-quality degradation paths first (model-variant throttle, reduced batch-size) before forced slot eviction. 3) Implement tenant soft-landing: an automated policy that routes affected requests to a compatible smaller model variant or to a 'degraded lane' with documented QoS. 4) Ship new telemetry signals and dashboards and tie automated alerts to the runway score.
design_decisions: Runway score computed as weighted sum: slot_hours (40%), queue_growth_rate (25%), kv_hit_delta (20%), recent_evictions (15%). Weights adjustable via runtime flags.
Evict only when runway_score < critical_threshold AND pool_utilization > pool_threshold to avoid oscillation.
Soft-landing options prioritized: model-variant downgrade -> smaller context-length config -> remote fallback tier. We avoid fallback to CPU-hosted variants unless degraded lane capacity confirmed.
Prefetch/ping logic: do not prefetch state for tenants in soft-landing to avoid further KV pollution.
Feature gated behind 'runway-stabilizer' FF for staged rollout and quick rollback.
Telemetry uses Prometheus metrics + new span attributes for per-request model-variant and kv-cache-hit-rate; dashboard in Console under 'Capacity / Runway'.
acceptance_criteria: Runway score metric emitted per-tenant and visible in Console dashboard.
Evictions from pools decreased by >= 40% in canary pool under synthetic surge tests compared to baseline eviction policy.
Canary rollout for 3 pools for 72 hours with automated rollback on increased tail latency or customer errors.
Automated alerts trigger when runway_score < warning_threshold for > 2 minutes for any tenant and on escalation when < critical_threshold.
Playbook updated with exact soft-landing steps and SRE runbook links.
Unit and e2e tests for the scoring function, eviction decision path, and soft-landing routing logic included in PRs.

rollout_plan: Stage 1 (Feature flag, internal dev cluster): validate scoring and no-op eviction path - 1 day
Stage 2 (Canary 3 hosted GPU pools): enable soft-landing routing only; monitor metrics for 72 hours; abort on error budget bleed - 7 days
Stage 3 (Gradual ramp): expand to 25% of pools with progressive thresholds; keep model downgrade list conservative - 14 days
Stage 4 (Global): enable default policy for all hosted pools after 2-week observation and formal sign-off from SRE and Product
telemetry_requirements: Per-tenant runway_score gauge (Prometheus) with labels: tenant_id, pool_id, model_family
Per-request span tags for model_variant, kv_cache_hit (bool), queue_wait_ms
Heatmap of kv_hit_rate delta over 1/5/15 minute windows to detect pollution patterns
Alerting: runway_warn (score < warn threshold for >2m), runway_crit (score < critical for >30s with pool_util > 85%)
test_plan: Unit tests for scoring weights and boundary conditions
Integration test: simulate tenant burst with varying KV hit patterns and assert runway_score trends as expected
Load test: controlled synthetic surge replicating Feb incident; measure eviction reduction and tail latency difference
Chaos test: flip FF during traffic to validate rollback safety
Canary validation checklist to be filled by SRE before wider rollout
notes: Design review 2026-03-04: PM asked to surface expected customer-visible degradation message and per-tenant credits behavior.
SRE feedback 2026-03-06: prefer conservative weight tuning and require canary with traffic replay rather than synthetic only.
Trade-off: soft-landing reduces immediate eviction but increases long-tail latency for degraded tenants; accepted for P1 safety net.
We will not automatically downgrade models that have explicit customer pinned-version settings unless tenant config allows it.
Follow-up: evaluate integrating with billing to avoid unexpected cost shifts for customers moved to remote tiers.
